name: query-explainer
description: Explains SQL you paste into the chat: what the query computes, step by step in plain English, the assumptions it silently makes (join matches, key uniqueness, NULL handling, time zones, tie-breaking) and its performance and correctness smells (a LEFT JOIN that became an inner join, NOT IN with NULLs, fan-out before SUM, functions on filtered columns, UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE). The SQL is parsed in code with sqlglot (PostgreSQL, MySQL, BigQuery, Snowflake, T-SQL, SQLite, Redshift, DuckDB, Oracle), so every finding is a rule tied to a fragment of your SQL; paste CREATE TABLE / CREATE INDEX statements and it confirms uniqueness and index questions from them. It never runs SQL, has no database access and never claims a query is slow. Follow-ups: explain only one CTE, assume a column is NOT NULL, suggest an untested rewrite, as json. Not for writing new queries, schema design or database administration.

skills.name: Explain a SQL query
skills.description: Plain-English steps of what pasted SQL computes, its hidden assumptions and its smells, each tied to a fragment of the SQL; pasted table definitions confirm keys and indexes. Read-only: SQL is parsed, never run.
examples: What does this UPDATE do? <paste the UPDATE and the CREATE TABLE>
Any problems with this BigQuery SQL? <paste SQL>
